Definition: from G4690 and G3004; a seed-picker (as the crow), i.e. (figuratively) a sponger, loafer (specially, a gossip or trifler in talk):--babbler.
BiblicalUsage: The babbler is what the philosophers of Athens called Paul: What will this seed-picker say? The word is a crow picking up scattered grain, turned into an insult for a man who picks up scraps of talk. They said it because he preached Jesus and the resurrection.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the insult is a compliment turned inside out: the man they called a scavenger was carrying the gospel.
